verdicts.note: 2 seeds/arm, vanilla block, same compute. Probe F1cls@0.2: frame kmaves 0.437±0.027 | oracle 0.361±0.009 | randseg 0.303±0.033; onset p50 50 | 64 | 74 ms. Full FT: 0.628±0.014 | 0.542±0.033 | 0.447±0.023; onset p50 34 | 44 | 56 ms. Paired bootstrap (seed 0, FT, tau .2): oracle - randseg +0.137 [+0.079,+0.206] P>0.999; frame - oracle +0.055 [-0.004,+0.105] P=0.968. Reading (pre-registered row 4): event-alignment recovers a large part of the loss caused by coarsening units to event length, but one-unit-per-event targets lose more than alignment returns, on plateau AND on boundaries. Causal claim limited to targets built by averaging AVES units over segments. Implication: an architecture that REPLACES fine units by event-level units is not supported; any boundary mechanism must be additive to fine units (hierarchy or auxiliary loss), and the simple competitor (frame units + auxiliary boundary loss) is now the first thing to test, not a learned segmenter

Clarification requested by the supervisor: the seed-mean gap frame-minus-oracle at FT is 0.086 (0.628 vs 0.542); the paired bootstrap +0.055 [-0.004,+0.105] is the SEED-0 pair only and its CI includes zero. statement: A JEPA formulation (separate 2-layer predictor, EMA target encoder, context encoder without masked tokens, block masks ~0.8 s) on the modern block beats modern data2vec at equal data and budget
contract: modern block, 20k steps x 32 x 5 s, seed 0 screening; compare to d2v_modern 0.466±0.031 probe / 0.647±0.012 FT and ft_scratch_modern 0.463

verdicts.note: Probe F1cls@0.2 0.276 (plateau 0.389, onset p50 76 ms) = vanilla data2vec level; FT 0.392, BELOW scratch-modern FT 0.463: block-mask JEPA pretraining harms initialisation. Hypothesised cause: 0.8 s blocks remove whole calls, which are not predictable from surrounding noise, so the predictor's task degenerates; short-span control (p .08, span 10, same predictor) queued to separate masking granularity from the predictor design

Rebuilt the run from the checkpoint and executed one step: predictor (3.7M, 27 tensors) is in the optimizer and receives gradients (norm 0.14 vs encoder 0.07); target encoder has no gradients; EMA moves the teacher after each step; masked context positions are exactly zero and unmasked are unchanged; targets instance-normed (std 1.00); loss computed on masked positions only (unmasked MSE 2.87 untrained, by design). Measured mask fraction 0.36 with mean block 45 tokens (0.9 s), not the ~45% I had assumed. Mechanically correct. Differences from our data2vec are THREE at once: (1) separate predictor with learned mask token instead of a linear head on the student output; (2) context encoder sees zeros at masked positions instead of a learned mask embedding; (3) target = last layer only instead of mean of top-4 layers. The screening therefore cannot attribute the loss to any one of them; the short-span control isolates only masking granularity. No further JEPA runs after that control; next hypothesis to be chosen jointly. Saved args lack jepa_p/jepa_span (flags added after the run); defaults 0.015/40 were used

same predictor/targets, HuBERT-style spans (p .08, span 10): probe 0.415 (plateau 0.537, onset 60 ms), FT 0.612 (onset 37 ms) vs block-mask 0.276 / 0.392 and d2v_modern 0.466±0.031 / 0.649±0.014. Masking granularity explains most of the block-mask loss (1 seed); with short spans the predictor formulation is still below data2vec but inside the pool. Supports the hypothesis that events are not predictable from context; does not establish that the predictor itself is harmful. No further JEPA runs

Teacher FT leads by ~0.04 recall at every budget; dev-selected thresholds overshoot the budget on test by 1.3-2x; recall is nearly flat across budgets, i.e. ~25% of calls never cross threshold (K12 recall 0.42-0.61 at 300/h). At the dev-100 FA/h point (test FAR 99 AVES / 79 d2v): AVES FT detected 75%, boundary-only 14% (84 events found but failing collar/offset tolerance), merged 6% (34), decoder 1%, below-threshold 2% (15), absent 2% (12); 'visible to Olga' (any overlap) 94.5%. data2vec modern: detected 71%, boundary-only 14%, merged 6%, below-threshold 5% (30), absent 4% (24); visible 90.5%. So (a) my claim 'a quarter of calls never cross threshold' was wrong: true non-detections are 5% (AVES) and 10% (student); the rest of the strict-scorer misses are found-but-mis-bounded or merged; (b) K12 is 18/152 = 12% of AVES misses, not the majority; (c) the AVES-student gap is in sensitivity (absent+below-threshold 27 vs 54 events), not in the decoder; (d) test recall-FAR curves are flat (AVES 0.75-0.77 over FAR 64-202/h; student 0.70-0.73), interpolated test recall at FAR 100: 0.761 vs 0.724. Examples exported for Olga

Boundary-only misses: 81% have a neighbouring reference within 0.3 s (median gap -0.06 s, i.e. overlapping annotations); merged: 100% (median gap -0.35 s); detected events: only 15%. Of the dense-bout misses ~40% have a different-class neighbour (splittable with class-aware tracks), ~60% same class (needs an explicit onset/overlap model). Identical pattern for AVES FT and the student. The class-agnostic call track saturates across abutting/overlapping calls and the two-threshold decoder emits one event; the strict scorer then counts all but one as misses. This, not sensitivity, is the dominant strict-recall loss (20% of references); sensitivity explains the AVES-student gap (27 vs 54 events)

verdicts.note: dev-budget 100 FA/h, 3 seeds per model. Student d2v+Gemma: base strict R 0.715±0.012 (test FAR 71, FAR-matched R@100 0.730) -> onset 0.755±0.012 (FAR 96, R@100 0.777, +0.047) ; class 0.745 but FAR 128 (+57/h), visible -0.007; both 0.772 but FAR 133, R@300 +0.075. Teacher AVES: base 0.754±0.008 (FAR 76, R@100 0.759) -> onset 0.821±0.004 (FAR 84, R@100 0.836, +0.077); class 0.804 at FAR 139; both 0.830 at FAR 140, R@300 +0.080. Onset split keeps or raises visible(>=50%) recall (+0.015 / +0.007) and halves boundary-only misses (70->54, 77->43); merged misses barely change (35->33, 38->34), i.e. onset split fixes abutting calls, not true overlaps. Class split raises FAR by ~60/h and lowers visibility, so its gain is not at matched FAR. Auxiliary onset loss did not change the base decoder (0.703 vs 0.706; 0.752 vs 0.752). Reading: stable improvement at comparable FAR with a clear source (dense-bout splitting); the pre-set +0.08 is met at FAR 300 for the teacher (both) and nearly at FAR 100 (onset, +0.077), +0.047 for the student. Mechanism is model-agnostic (FT-stage head + decoder); not yet run on modern HuBERT (km(AVES) modern) - porting is a 6-min FT per seed and is the open decision

dev-100 operating points, 2000 resamples of 17 recordings, seeds pooled. Student (3 seeds): onset vs base +0.039 [+0.012,+0.079] strict recall, visible(>=50%) +0.015 [+0.007,+0.025]; onset vs plain FT (no aux head) +0.045 [-0.003,+0.107]; aux loss alone +0.006 [-0.022,+0.035]. Teacher (seeds 0,1 matched): onset vs base +0.071 [+0.028,+0.111], visible +0.010 [+0.004,+0.016]; onset vs plain FT +0.078 [+0.025,+0.130]; aux alone +0.007 [-0.012,+0.023]. False alarms rise with onset split (student 261->350 summed over 3 seeds, teacher 198->221 over 2), so operating-point deltas are not FAR-matched; the FAR-matched curve gives +0.047 / +0.077 at 100 FA/h. The gain is in splitting found series (strict recall), coverage gains are 0.01-0.015. Nearest prior work: Voxaboxen (Mahon, Hoffman et al., DCASE 2025) - onset/offset boxes with duration regression on an AVES backbone, graph-matched, robust to overlap, already 65.5 sed_eval F1 on these recordings; YOHO (2022) start/end regression; SEBBs (Ebbers 2024). Our mechanism is a one-logit auxiliary onset head used only to split two-threshold events: simpler, keeps the frame-wise operating point, but is a subset of what Voxaboxen does. Missing comparison: Voxaboxen under our recall-at-FAR protocol

statement: Voxaboxen (published onset/offset box detector, BEATs backbone, trained only on synthetic recordings from lab clips) under our recall-at-FAR protocol, from its stored per-recording predictions (no training)
contract: stored fwd/bck boxes with Detection Prob >= 0.5 (tool pre-filter), fusion approximated as fwd + non-overlapping bck (IoU<0.5); threshold sweep only upward from 0.5; same 17 recordings, class-agnostic matching tau 0.5
expect: reference point for the onset-split component

verdicts.note: fused @0.5: test FAR 61/h, strict recall 0.816, coverage>=50% 0.938, boundary-only 33, merged 56; sed_eval 62.6 with my fusion vs 65.5 reported with the tool's graph matching, so the real system is somewhat stronger. Our best onset-split models: teacher 0.821 at FAR 84, student 0.755 at FAR 96; at ~60 FA/h our teacher base is ~0.75. Voxaboxen never saw field audio while our FT models used train-fold field labels. Its curve below thr 0.5 is unavailable (pre-filtered), so dev-budget rows at <=50 FA/h are truncation artefacts. Its remaining misses are dominated by true overlaps (merged 56) rather than boundary failures (33). Conclusion: the published onset-based detector beats the one-head split at matched FAR; the contribution of our section is the miss decomposition, not a competitive detector

statement: Prototype: modern HuBERT that keeps frame-level units and adds an event-instance branch (presence, onset, log-duration; overlapping instances allowed) trained already during pretraining on synthetic mixtures whose inserted-call positions are known by construction, then fine-tuned on train-fold field labels. Joint training of units and event structure reduces absorptions/boundary failures more than adding the instance head only at FT
contract: modern block, 20k steps; regimes R1 units only (existing kmaves_modern ckpts), R2 units + event branch (ev_w 1: BCE presence + BCE onset pw10 + 0.5 L1 log-duration), R3 event branch only (control); identical FT with the same instance head (1.5k steps) and identical instance decoder (onset peaks + predicted duration, overlaps allowed) tuned on dev under FAR<=100/h; 3 seeds each. Explicitly extra supervision from the synthetic construction, not pure SSL
expect: R2 > R1 on strict recall at matched test FAR and on the overlapping-reference subset; R3 shows whether the unit loss matters at all
limits: close to Voxaboxen (onset + duration on an SSL backbone): novelty, if any, lies in training the instance branch during pretraining on construction labels and in keeping frame units; to be compared against Voxaboxen under the same protocol

verdicts.status: outcome: joint objective NOT better than the event-only control; event-instance pretraining and the instance decoder carry the gain
verdicts.note: Instance decoder, dev<=100 FA/h, mean+-sd over 3 seeds: R1 (units only, head at FT) strict R 0.799+-0.005 at test FAR 90; R2 (units + event branch) 0.871+-0.012 at FAR 106; R3 (event branch only, no unit loss) 0.887+-0.029 at FAR 128. FAR-matched at 100/h: 0.801 / 0.873 / 0.885. Overlapping-reference subset (n=119): 0.638 / 0.723 / 0.709. Paired recording-level bootstrap (B=2000, recording carries all seeds), dR at FAR 100: R2-R1 +0.065 [+0.038,+0.095]; R3-R1 +0.083 [+0.043,+0.124]; R3-R2 +0.015 [-0.007,+0.038] (overlap subset -0.014 [-0.045,+0.011]). So (i) pretraining the instance branch on construction labels beats adding it only at FT (+0.065), (ii) the HuBERT unit loss adds nothing measurable on top of it, the event-only control is at least as good, also with the frame decoder (R3-R1 frame +0.030 [+0.006,+0.060]). (iii) The instance decoder itself is the largest effect: vs the frame decoder on the same runs +0.11 (R1) to +0.17 (R2/R3) at FAR 100, overlap-subset recall 0.24 -> 0.72. Voxaboxen (stored boxes, thr>=0.5 only, never saw field audio): at its maximal FAR 61/h R 0.816; R2 at 61/h 0.847, R3 0.849; paired dR +0.044 [-0.046,+0.166] / +0.039 [-0.051,+0.150], not resolved (Voxaboxen's single low-FAR point, wide CI); at the dev-100 operating point it reaches only 0.697 at FAR 43. Caveats: R2/R3 operating FARs overshoot the dev budget (106/128 vs 90), so matched-FAR numbers are the primary ones; R3 FAR-matched R@100 defined in all bootstrap samples, R2 in 66%; the event branch uses construction labels (supervised pretraining on synthetic mixtures), so the result says synthetic instance supervision > masked-unit SSL for this detector, not 'a better HuBERT'. Files: results/bootstrap_instances_b100.json, results/decode_instances_fte_R*_seed*_b100.json. UPDATE (wider threshold grid, th_on down to 0.005, R@100 now defined in >=99% of bootstrap samples): R2-R1 +0.066 [+0.038,+0.096]; R3-R1 +0.086 [+0.045,+0.128]; R3-R2 +0.019 [-0.004,+0.042]; instance-frame +0.157 (R2) / +0.102 (R1). Wording per supervisor: 'additional benefit of the HuBERT objective not detected in H21', not 'unnecessary'. 0.072 (seed means at dev operating points, FAR 106 vs 90) vs 0.066 (pooled FAR-matched curve, bootstrap mean) = different quantity and aggregation (check_aggregation.py); the pooled full-data estimate is 0.068.

statement: Does the modern (Gemma-style) block matter for the event-only detector (R3)? R3 on the vanilla block vs R3 modern, same FT and instance decoder.
contract: pretrain.py --variant kmaves --block vanilla --event_head --no_hubert, seed 0 only (screening); finetune --block vanilla --event_head; decode_instances dev<=100; compare with fte_R3_seed0 (modern) via paired recording bootstrap; repeats only if the difference deserves it
expect: screening: if vanilla matches modern, the modern block has no measurable role in the event detector under this budget (this component combination only); if vanilla is worse, the block contributes and component attribution becomes a question
limits: one seed; closes only this combination of components at this compute budget, not all ways of modernising HuBERT

verdicts.status: screening (seed 0): vanilla block worse than modern in the event-only detector
verdicts.note: Instance decoder, dev<=100: vanilla op R 0.869 at FAR 146 vs modern 0.905 at FAR 132; R@100 from pooled test curve 0.847 vs 0.890. Paired recording bootstrap (seed 0 only): dR op -0.036 [-0.062,-0.011]; dR@100 -0.063 [-0.161,-0.022]; dR@150 -0.054 [-0.107,-0.024]; overlapping subset +0.017 [-0.045,+0.073] (no difference). Frame decoder: -0.022 [-0.067,+0.018], unresolved. Caveat: modern seed 0 is the best of its three seeds (0.905; others 0.902, 0.853), vanilla 0.869 lies inside the modern seed range, so one seed cannot settle it; seeds 1,2 queued after the Voxaboxen run (run_r3van_seeds.sh). Pretraining event loss at 20k: vanilla 0.52 vs modern 0.33 (same data), consistent with the block mattering for the event branch.

verdicts.status: 3 seeds: vanilla block worse than modern in the event-only detector (every seed lower)
verdicts.note: Instance decoder, dev<=100: vanilla per-seed op recall 0.869/0.825/0.786 (pooled 0.827 at FAR 101) vs modern 0.905/0.902/0.853 (0.887 at FAR 128); pooled test-curve R@61/100/150: vanilla 0.792/0.844/0.853 vs modern 0.849/0.885/0.903. Paired recording bootstrap (recording carries all seeds): dR op -0.060 [-0.079,-0.039]; dR@100 -0.050 [-0.114,-0.018]; dR@150 -0.049 [-0.076,-0.026]; dR@61 -0.061 [-0.162,+0.001]; overlapping subset -0.068 [-0.103,-0.036]. Frame decoder: op -0.021 [-0.037,-0.005], R@100 -0.021 [-0.043,+0.000] (borderline). Reading: the modern (Gemma-style) block contributes measurably to the event-instance detector, more than it did to the frame detector with HuBERT units (H1x: ~0); closes only this component combination (RMSNorm+GeGLU+RoPE+QK-norm+local/global attention+gated conv together) at this compute budget; which component matters is not attributed. Files: results/bootstrap_h22_b100.json.

statement: Field-fine-tuned Voxaboxen (BEATs, from its synthetic-trained detector) under our protocol: same folds/dev, same access to field labels, staff decoder (soft-NMS + fwd/bck bipartite matching), threshold under FA budgets; vs R2/R3 instance detectors
contract: voxaboxen 0.2.0 (commit 20cf966) with 4 local inference patches; per fold: train-model from final-model.pt, April-2026 hyperparameters, n_epochs 50 early stopping on dev (patience 10); inference det 0.05, comb_discard 0, Detection Prob swept; seed 0 only; paired recording bootstrap vs R1/R2/R3 at 61/100/150/300 FA/h
expect: decides competitiveness of the instance detector against the nearest published method at equal data access

verdicts.status: budget-dependent: ours ahead at <=100 FA/h and on overlapping calls; parity/behind at >=150 FA/h
verdicts.note: VOXFT dev<=100: strict R 0.773 at test FAR 91 (thresholds 0.7/0.75/0.8), overlapping-subset 0.479, coverage 0.830; FAR-matched R@61/100/150/300 = 0.695/0.790/0.868/0.945. Paired: R2-VOXFT op +0.096 [+0.050,+0.135]; R@61 +0.142 [+0.046,+0.262]; R@100 +0.076 [-0.014,+0.176] (not resolved); R@150 +0.019 [-0.059,+0.112]; R@300 -0.031 [-0.077,+0.019] (R2 curve rarely reaches 300). R3-VOXFT: op +0.112 [+0.063,+0.153]; R@61 +0.141 [+0.053,+0.247]; R@100 +0.095 [+0.010,+0.184]; R@150 +0.038 [-0.034,+0.128]; R@300 -0.024 [-0.058,+0.019]. Overlapping subset: +0.244 [+0.168,+0.344] (R2), +0.230 [+0.167,+0.306] (R3). R1-VOXFT: R@100 +0.009 n.s., R@300 -0.121 [-0.174,-0.062] (units-only student loses at high budgets). VOXFT vs synthetic-only VOX at 61 FA/h: -0.121 [-0.204,-0.044] (field FT lowered its low-FAR recall) while raising high-FAR recall. Caveats: one Voxaboxen seed; its training ran ~48-50 epochs with the best model found late (fold0/1/2 best at epochs see log), i.e. capped by the matched budget, possibly under-trained; encoder 90M vs our 17.8M; its dev-chosen comb_discard irrelevant here because the curve is swept. Reading: at Olga's budgets (<=100 FA/h) and for overlapping calls the instance detector leads with CIs excluding zero (R3 at 100; both at 61); at >=150 FA/h Voxaboxen-FT catches up and is nominally ahead at 300 (unresolved). Files: results/voxft_b100.json, results/bootstrap_instances_b100.json.

verdicts.status: best-val checkpoint variant is weaker than the staff last-epoch model; conclusion unchanged
verdicts.note: Second pass with a local patch saving best-model.pt whenever val comb-F1 improves (best epochs 19/42/25): op 0.685 at FAR 76, overlap 0.445, coverage 0.737; R@61/100/150/300 = 0.653/0.764/0.842/0.935, i.e. below the last-epoch model everywhere (VOXFTB-VOXFT R@61 -0.043 [-0.089,+0.001], R@100 -0.024 [-0.057,+0.006]). The 'overfit last epoch' objection is dismissed: val-F1 selection picks a precision-oriented epoch that is worse under recall-at-FAR. Paired vs best-val variant: R2 R@61 +0.185 [+0.092,+0.286], R@100 +0.101 [+0.019,+0.199], R@150 +0.039 [-0.034,+0.119], R@300 -0.011 [-0.061,+0.054]; R3 R@100 +0.119 [+0.043,+0.204]; overlap +0.27/+0.28. Headline for the paper uses the stronger Voxaboxen variant (last epoch, staff pipeline). Files: results/voxftb_b100.json, results/bootstrap_instances_b100.json.

verdicts.status: wording corrected after supervisor review; overlap recall at matched FAR added
verdicts.note: Supervisor: field FT degraded Voxaboxen at <=61 FA/h (0.695 vs synthetic 0.816), so '+0.141' is over a degraded configuration; vs synthetic checkpoint R3 +0.033 (CI includes 0) → claim = 'beats the tested field-FT configuration of Voxaboxen', not 'beats the method'; a recall-FAR-appropriate FT regime for Voxaboxen was not found. Bipartite fwd/bck matching does not forbid overlapping outputs; soft-NMS is the candidate; explanation remains a hypothesis. Overlap recall at matched FAR (new): R3 vs VOXFT @100 +0.195 [+0.020,+0.304], @61 +0.248 [+0.139,+0.352]; vs VOX @61 +0.160 [+0.060,+0.248]; R2-R1 @100 +0.068 [+0.025,+0.112]; inst-frame @100 +0.415. Synthetic overlap fraction corrected: 57% of calls overlap another call (event-level, 1500 clips), not 37%.

statement: Does overlap in the synthetic construction explain the instance detector's gain on overlapping field calls? R3 (event branch only, modern) pretrained on a no-overlap synthetic corpus vs the default corpus
contract: TSSSL_NOOVERLAP=1 in common.synth: same clip ids, gains and call-count draws as the default corpus, calls placed only in free segments (min gap 0.1 s), unplaceable calls dropped; measured on 1500 clips: calls/clip 2.38 vs 2.51, overlapping-call fraction 0.00 vs 0.57 (event-level definition), call-time 0.44 vs 0.38; pretraining 20k steps, 3 seeds; identical FT (field labels unchanged) and instance decoder; compare with fte_R3_seed0-2 via paired recording bootstrap; primary readout = recall on the overlapping-reference subset (n=119), secondary = R@100 and isolated-subset recall
expect: if the overlapping-subset gain shrinks on the no-overlap corpus, the overlap-rich construction is a measured difference from Voxaboxen's sequential synthetic data; if not, the gain is attributable to the decoder/branch alone
limits: corpus differs slightly in call density (-5% calls, +6 pp call time); one architecture (R3)

verdicts.status: 3 seeds: without overlaps in the synthetic pretraining corpus the overlapping-subset recall drops by 0.11 at matched FAR, isolated recall unchanged; the instance-decoder advantage on overlaps persists at about two thirds of its size
verdicts.note: Instance decoder, dev<=100: no-overlap per-seed op recall 0.876/0.840/0.825 (pooled 0.847 at FAR 111) vs default 0.905/0.902/0.853 (0.887 at FAR 128); pooled test curve R@61/100/150: 0.810/0.854/0.872 vs 0.849/0.885/0.903. Overlapping subset (n=119) at matched FAR 100: 0.600 vs 0.708; at 61: 0.518 vs 0.633; isolated subset at FAR 100: 0.916 vs 0.928. Paired recording bootstrap (B=2000, recording carries all seeds), no-overlap minus default: overlap@100 -0.110 [-0.169,-0.057], overlap@61 -0.110 [-0.154,-0.058], overlap@150 -0.109 [-0.170,-0.064]; isolated@100 -0.015 [-0.042,+0.004] (no difference); R@100 -0.033 [-0.066,-0.010]; op recall -0.040 [-0.052,-0.027]. Within the no-overlap model the instance decoder still beats the frame decoder on overlaps: +0.270 [+0.160,+0.366] at FAR 100 (default corpus: +0.422 [+0.273,+0.528]). Frame decoder of the same models is slightly BETTER on the no-overlap corpus (+0.038 [+0.010,+0.069] at FAR 100), so the loss is specific to the instance pathway, not to representation quality. Reading: overlaps in the synthetic construction are a measured contributor to overlap recall (about a quarter of the instance-vs-frame overlap advantage, 0.11 of 0.42), specific to overlapping calls; the larger part of the advantage comes from the event branch + instance decoder (and field FT labels, which contain overlaps in both arms). Explains the result; not a novelty claim (published Voxaboxen also trains on overlap-rich synthetic sets). Limits: corpus density differs slightly (-5% calls, +6 pp call time); one architecture (R3 modern); the frame-decoder gain on the no-overlap corpus shows the corpora are not perfectly matched.

statement: Does the one-token/one-instance limitation of the event branch (one onset peak and one duration per 20 ms token; two calls starting in the same token cannot both be represented) explain a notable share of the remaining misses on overlapping calls? Analysis only, no training.
contract: analyze_onset_proximity.py on fte_R3_seed0-2 at the dev<=100 instance operating points: for each missed overlapping reference, distance from its onset to the nearest other reference onset; categories same-token (<=20 ms), within the fold's chosen d_min (peak suppressed by minimum peak distance), other (split by whether an onset peak >=0.05 exists within +-1 token of the reference onset)
expect: if same-token misses are a large share, a multi-instance-per-token output (slots/queries) is a motivated architectural direction; if not, that direction is not supported by the error structure
limits: R3 only; operating points differ per fold/seed; 119 overlapping references

verdicts.status: diagnostic: onset collisions are rare (6% of missed overlapping calls have another onset within 20 ms) and do not motivate a multi-instance-per-token output as the next priority
verdicts.note: Per run: 119 overlapping refs, 34.7 missed (recall 0.709). Nearest other onset for the missed ones: <=20 ms (same token) 2.0 (6%); within the chosen d_min (0.2-0.7 s depending on fold/seed) 10.0 (29%): the second onset peak is suppressed by the minimum peak distance, which the dev selection set to 0.2-0.3 s under the FA budget although 0.1 s was in the grid, i.e. a precision trade-off, not a representational limit; other 22.7 (65%), of which 12.7 have an onset peak >=0.05 at the reference onset (peak present but instance failed score/boundary matching) and 10.0 have no onset evidence (sensitivity). Only 3% of all overlapping references have another onset within 20 ms (6% of the missed ones), so a multi-instance-per-token output could recover at most ~2 references per run. Reading: the slot/query architecture direction is not motivated by the measured error structure; the remaining overlap misses are peak suppression under the FA budget, boundary/score failures and sensitivity. No architecture work follows from this. WORDING (supervisor 2026-10-20): this is a diagnostic breakdown by onset proximity, not a proof of causes or an upper bound on improvement; 'onsets within 20 ms' is not identical to 'same token'; the suppression by d_min is a real suppression step of the decoder, so the manuscript says 'no IoU-based box suppression / no NMS of boxes', not 'no suppression step'.

statement: Does the C6/H24 effect transfer to another species and public data? On OZF (Overlapping Zebra Finch, Zenodo 15507508): R3 pretrained on paired synthetic corpora with vs without overlaps (identical call lists), identical FT and decoder; does recall on overlapping real test calls drop without overlaps while the frame-wise track does not degrade?
contract: TSSSL_OZF_protocol_ru.md (fixed before launch): official split train46/val6/test13, slow-down x2 by sample-rate trick, lab corpus from train only, paired corpora TSSSL_PAIRED=1 (5.36 calls/mix, overlap 0.389 vs 0), R3 modern event-only 20k steps x 3 seeds x 2 arms, FT 1.5k steps on train, thresholds on val under 400 FA per slowed hour, tau 0.1 s slowed, matched FAR 200/400/800, paired bootstrap over 13 test recordings; secondary: six synthetic test sets by inference, mAP@0.5/0.8 by Voxaboxen code, optional Voxaboxen run on OZF train
expect: replication: overlap recall lower without synthetic overlaps (interval excludes zero) and frame decoder not worse -> transferable training-data-construction effect; otherwise a boundary of applicability, reported as such
limits: one additional dataset; synthetic density chosen to match OZF; no hyperparameter search

verdicts.status: NOT found on OZF: no detectable difference between the paired overlap and no-overlap pretraining corpora in recall (overall, overlapping, isolated) for either decoder; mAP means differ but were not bootstrapped; instance-vs-frame replicates with a large margin; label amount is one of several candidate explanations (durations, acoustics, pretraining clip origin), none varied in isolation
verdicts.note: Real OZF test (13 recordings, 1744 refs, 548 overlapping), val-chosen thresholds under 400 FA per slowed hour, 3 seeds per arm. Instance decoder op: with overlaps 0.933 [0.916,0.951] at FAR 265, overlap subset 0.823, isolated 0.984; without overlaps 0.938 [0.924,0.954] at FAR 255, overlap 0.831, isolated 0.988. Per seed (ov) 0.933/0.929/0.938, overlap 0.828/0.812/0.828; (noov) 0.937/0.944/0.935, overlap 0.821/0.839/0.832. Paired noov-ov: op recall +0.005 [-0.004,+0.014]; op overlap +0.006 [-0.024,+0.031]; op isolated +0.004 [-0.000,+0.009]; at matched FAR 200/slowed h (81% of resamples defined): R +0.003 [-0.007,+0.013], overlap -0.005 [-0.038,+0.026], isolated +0.007 [+0.001,+0.013]. Curves do not reach 400 or 800 FA/h in >99% of resamples (instance decoder saturates at FAR ~300 with the lowest threshold), so 200 is the only matched point. Frame decoder: 0.567 vs 0.575, overlap 0.117 vs 0.125, differences +0.008 [-0.002,+0.018] / +0.007 [-0.007,+0.020]: no difference either. Instance - frame (same models): +0.364 [+0.311,+0.416] overall, +0.705 [+0.664,+0.746] on overlapping calls, +0.210 isolated (op points; frame FAR 660 vs instance 260). Six synthetic OZF test sets (inference only, frozen thresholds; a different domain: denoised calls at SNR -15..0 dB, recall 0.34-0.62): both arms degrade with the overlap ratio similarly; no-overlap arm equal or better except at ratio 1 (0.336 vs 0.362, op points with different FAR). mAP in Voxaboxen's definition (real time, test split): ov 90.6/91.3/91.7 @0.5 and 55.9/55.2/57.7 @0.8; noov 92.3/92.7/91.7 and 53.6/51.3/53.3; Voxaboxen published on OZF 97.92 / 81.23 -> our compact detector is behind under mAP, strongly so at IoU 0.8 (box precision at 10 ms real token grid). Reading: C6 is a boundary of applicability, not a transferable effect: on OZF the fine-tuning labels are abundant (5514 train calls, 32% overlapping) against ~400 per fold on the whale data, and both arms reach the same ceiling; the instance pathway effect (C3) transfers. BUG FOUND AND FIXED during this analysis: decode_instances.py divided the test FAR by the hours of dev+test recordings (correct for whale where every recording is a test recording in some fold; wrong for the single OZF split: FAR printed as 197 instead of 288 for seed 0); dev threshold selection and the bootstrap were unaffected; whale outputs re-verified identical after the fix. Pending: Voxaboxen trained on OZF train under its staff script, scored by our recall@FAR protocol.

verdicts.status: Voxaboxen trained on OZF: close recall at matched FAR, difference not established (overall interval within about 0.02; on overlapping calls up to 0.07 either way); Voxaboxen scores higher in mAP@0.8 (worse quality of our detections under strict interval agreement)
verdicts.note: Under our protocol (val threshold 0.6 under 400 FA/slowed h): test recall 0.929 at FAR 196, overlap 0.796; matched R@200/400 0.930/0.935, overlap 0.796/0.799. mAP from the same boxes (our computation of their definition, real time): 92.30 @0.5, 67.09 @0.8 (published 97.92/81.23 with the authors' pipeline). Paired vs R3 overlap-arm (13 recordings): op recall +0.004 [-0.009,+0.019] (our FAR higher by 69), op overlap +0.028 [-0.015,+0.082], R@200 -0.004 [-0.017,+0.012], OV@200 +0.014 [-0.029,+0.070]; vs no-overlap arm: R@200 -0.000 [-0.016,+0.016], OV@200 +0.009 [-0.043,+0.068], OV@400 +0.042 [+0.006,+0.083]. Reading: on OZF our 17.8M detector equals the 90M Voxaboxen in recall at matched FAR, including overlapping calls, and trails it in box precision (mAP@0.8 55 vs 67); the whale low-FAR advantage is not a general superiority. Files: results/voxozf_b400.json, voxozf_counts.npz, bootstrap_ozf_vox_b400.json, vox_ozf_eval.py, bootstrap_ozf_vox.py, run_vox_ozf.sh.
